examples.label: Download a real module to backdoor
Trigger the planted shell after installing the module

notes: Backdooring a legit module (adding shell.php + a permissive .htaccess) is the go-to when the PHP filter is unavailable. The .htaccess is required so Apache will execute PHP under /modules.

recommended.note: Simpler path on older Drupal with the PHP filter.

name: Drupal - Backdoored Module Upload
command:
# add shell.php + .htaccess to a module, repackage, install
mv shell.php .htaccess captcha
tar cvf captcha.tar.gz captcha/
description: Downloads a legitimate module, injects a PHP webshell plus a .htaccess to allow execution, repackages it, and installs it via Extend > Install new module for RCE.

variations.label: Create webshell via base64 decode (alternative to embedding in module)
